lede.headline: Kering's Gucci problem keeps getting worse
lede.dek: Gucci's comparable sales fell 6% in the third quarter, worse than Wall Street expected, and Kering's US-listed shares tumbled more than 12% in a single day.

stories.headline: Spotify shares jump on a subscriber beat
stories.move: Spotify said Thursday its premium subscribers reached 306 million in the third quarter, a million more than the company's own guidance and above analyst estimates. Revenue was roughly €5 billion, in line with forecasts, though earnings per share missed estimates. Shares rose about 10% to 11% that day.
stories.why: The subscriber beat reassured investors that Spotify's growth is intact even after a rocky year for the stock, with co-CEOs Gustav Soderstrom and Alex Norstrom running day-to-day operations under Ek's oversight as executive chairman.
stories.bear: The earnings-per-share miss shows margin pressure persists, and the jump partly reflects a stock that had fallen sharply earlier in the year.
stories.watch: Spotify's fourth-quarter guidance of roughly 316 million premium subscribers.

stories.headline: SpaceX stock falls despite a profitable quarter
stories.move: SpaceX reported about $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 161% from a year earlier, but shares fell 9.1% on Thursday. Capital expenditures topped $16 billion, and management projected $35 billion to $40 billion in fourth-quarter capex, pointing to negative free cash flow.
stories.why: Investors focused on how SpaceX will fund its AI and Starlink buildout, and on lingering uncertainty over the still-preliminary talks about a possible merger with Tesla, where no terms have been set.
stories.bear: The 161% revenue growth and the swing to a profit are real, and some of the drop reflects profit-taking after the stock had jumped the prior session.
stories.watch: Whether SpaceX and Tesla's special committees reach merger terms before Tesla's annual meeting.

stories.headline: Marvell slides as a chip-equipment maker flags supply strain
stories.move: Marvell Technology shares fell about 8% on Thursday after chipmaking-equipment supplier Lam Research said on its Oct. 21 earnings call that near-term supply-chain constraints would otherwise have lifted its revenue guidance. AMD and Intel also fell that day, down about 8% and 7%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped 6%.
stories.why: Lam's comments raised worries that supply limits, not demand, could cap how fast AI-chip makers like Marvell can grow, after a stretch of steep valuations across the sector.
stories.bear: Lam's own executives said the constraints should ease, with CEO Tim Archer predicting the industry will be "caught up very shortly."
stories.watch: Marvell's next earnings report for signs the supply strain is easing.

stories.headline: Blackstone shares rise on record assets under management
stories.move: Blackstone said Thursday that its net profit fell from a year earlier, but assets under management hit a record $1.35 trillion, up 11%, and distributable earnings reached $1.52 a share, which funds its dividend. Shares rose as much as 4% in early trading.
stories.why: The results showed Blackstone's fundraising machine still working even as some rivals have struggled, with inflows exceeding $260 billion over the past year.
stories.bear: Fee-related earnings growth of 22% is strong, but much of the AUM gain reflects market appreciation and new commitments rather than realized returns paid out to investors.
stories.watch: Whether Blackstone's promised pickup in asset sales materializes in the fourth quarter.

stories.headline: AMD falls with the broader chip sell-off
stories.move: AMD shares fell about 8% on Thursday, one of several chip stocks sliding after Lam Research's chief financial officer said on an Oct. 21 earnings call that near-term supply-chain constraints were holding back its own revenue guidance. Marvell and Intel also fell, down about 8% and 7%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped 6%.
stories.why: The comments from a key chip-equipment supplier raised concern that the AI buildout could be slowed by supply limits, adding to a run of volatile sessions for AMD and its peers.
stories.bear: Lam's executives said the constraints are expected to ease, and shipments slipping out of this quarter are expected to ship in the next.
stories.watch: AMD's own next earnings report for guidance on data-center demand.

stories.headline: Meta tops revenue forecasts despite a big legal charge
stories.move: Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% from a year earlier and above analyst estimates of about $63.3 billion. Earnings per share were $3.83, including a $9.9 billion charge tied to its settlement with state attorneys general; excluding that charge, per-share earnings would have been $7.40. Shares rose about 2% in after-hours trading on Oct. 21.
stories.why: The revenue beat showed Meta's advertising business still growing fast even as the company piles up AI-related costs, a question investors have pressed management on all year.
stories.bear: The legal charge and heavy capital spending cut deeply into profit, and Meta forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, a wide range that leaves room to disappoint.
stories.watch: Meta's updated capital-spending outlook for next year, which management has signaled could top this year's levels.

stories.headline: SoftBank shares slide as AI debt worries deepen
stories.move: SoftBank Group shares fell sharply on Thursday, leaving the stock roughly half of its June peak, as worries deepened about the sustainability of its large AI bets, including its stakes in Arm and OpenAI. Credit-default swaps on SoftBank's debt climbed to their highest level in years.
stories.why: Investors have grown more skeptical that SoftBank's AI investments will generate returns fast enough to cover the debt used to fund them, after reports questioned OpenAI's actual revenue run rate.
stories.bear: SoftBank's holdings in Arm and OpenAI still carry enormous paper value, and founder Masayoshi Son has said he expects market corrections to be the best buying opportunities.
stories.watch: SoftBank's next update on its OpenAI commitment and credit-rating outlook.

stories.headline: Reliance's Jio Platforms opens India's biggest-ever IPO
stories.move: Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital-services arm of Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries, opened its initial public offering on Oct. 21 and closed it on Oct. 23. The fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares was reported to carry a price band of roughly 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share, which could raise around $3.2 billion at the top end.
stories.why: The listing is India's largest-ever IPO and a major test of investor appetite for the country's telecom and digital-services market, which Ambani has built into one of Reliance's fastest-growing units.
stories.bear: The final issue price and demand level were not yet confirmed in public filings at the time of reporting.
stories.watch: Jio Platforms' expected listing date on Indian exchanges, reported around Oct. 28.

quickHits: Nvidia and Micron also fell in Thursday's chip sell-off, down more than 4% and 6%, as Lam Research's supply-chain comments weighed on the sector.
memo: A supplier's cautious words can move an entire industry: Lam Research's supply-chain comment wiped billions off Marvell, AMD and Intel in a single session.
Beating on revenue isn't enough if costs run ahead of it: Meta's ad business grew 26%, but a legal charge and AI spending still cut into profit.
A turnaround takes longer to prove than to promise: two years into Gucci's fix, Kering's comparable sales are still falling, just more slowly.

movers.why: Spotify rose 11.1% after the company said premium subscribers reached 306 million, above its own forecast.
SpaceX fell 9.1% as investors weighed its AI capex needs and uncertainty around a possible Tesla merger.
Marvell fell 8.7% after Lam Research warned of supply-chain constraints limiting chip-equipment shipments.
AMD fell 8.1% after Lam Research's supply-chain warning deepened a broader chip-stock sell-off.
Blackstone rose 8.4% after the company reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street's profit estimate.
